newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steel makers' shares up on investor hopes.
newsitem.headline: Japan steel makers' shares up on investor hopes.

text.p: Shares in Japanese steel makers were slightly higher on Wednesday morning, due to hopes that the sector will flourish after the bullish bond market takes a breather and investors re-direct their funds to large capital shares in the stock market, brokers said.
As of 0113 GMT, Kawasaki Steel Corp was up three yen at 344 yen. Trade volume was 1.328 million shares, the sixth heaviest on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
NKK Corp was one yen higher at 284 yen. Nisshin Steel Co Ltd rose two to 361 yen.
"Once the bond market calms down, funds will come pouring back into the stock market," Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities, said.

"Investors will need to buy large-capital issues to use up their vast funds as they can't go through the tedious procedure of buying small, individual issues," he added. "Some speculative investors are moving ahead of everyone else today."
